instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Check that every place declared writable (on the promise that something keeps what is written there, such as a version history) really keeps it, and say which keep nothing", and give it places_key; id_key; retention_kinds.
2. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:check-declared-places-keep-what-is-written-there and its input (the worked example shows one).

3. Read what comes back: Give the declaration (the JSON that lists the places, or declaration_file, a path inside the folder the person granted for reading), places_key (the key that holds the list, found at any depth), id_key (the key naming each place), bases (folders inside the granted folder a place may live under; "" is the folder itself) and retention_kinds ([{ kind, marker }]: a kind keeps what is written when its marker, a file or folder name such as a history folder, is present at the place or any ancestor up to the granted folder).
